newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia employers, unions extend benefit accord.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia employers, unions extend benefit accord.

text.p: Slovenian trade unions and employers on Monday signed an amendment to their general collective agreement, prolonging an accord determining work benefits until the end of May 1997.

"The amendment will enable us to start negotiations on work benefits by securing the current accord until the end of May," Dusan Semolic, head of Slovenia's largest trade union the Association of Free Trade Unions (ZSSS), told Reuters.
In October, Slovenia's Chamber of Economy and Association of Employers pushed for changes to the collective agreement from January next year, sparking a brief general strike in October.

The chamber suggested the agreement, which was introduced in 1990 and renewed in 1993, should be amended to reduce daily allowances, holiday and sick pay, redundancy payments and strike compensation in financially troubled companies.

"Negotiations will be tough because the employers' proposal is unacceptable. We are strongly opposed to a suggested cut in sick pay to 60 percent of net from 80 percent and the abolition of holiday pay," Semolic said.

"We believe employers should take other steps to improve the competitiveness of Slovenian companies, namely by looking for new markets and improving management, work organisation and marketing," he added.
